consensus_summary: Biblical 'to know' (yada/ginōskō) primarily denotes intimate, experiential, covenantal relationship and personal communion (esp. with God), distinct from mere intellectual awareness; sexual union is the paradigm case, with common extensions to election/foreknowledge, obedience as evidence or ethical conduct, and moral experience.
book_summary: Covenant relationship proven by obedience — the intimate “knew” of marriage; a stranger is one not known.
book_core_identification: covenant relationship proven by obedience (intimate marriage paradigm; stranger = not known)
boundary_disagreement: Book makes 'proven by obedience' definitional to the covenant relationship (narrowing via 1 John/Hosea), while consensus treats relational intimacy itself as primary and obedience as one common expression/evidence among others (election, pure communion, moral experience); pure relational or elective cases without the proof emphasis are less central or reclassified.
material_contradiction: None — book retains the intimate covenant/relational core (shared Gen 4:1 marriage paradigm and Matt 7:23 non-knowing) without denying or replacing it.
rationale: Minimum cores align on intimate covenant relationship (marriage 'knew' as model, stranger contrast). Book preserves that referent/category but materially narrows precision and boundary conditions by elevating 'proven by obedience' to the identification itself (drawing 1 John 2:3-4 and Hos 4:6 into the core), excluding or de-emphasizing broader consensus cases of relational knowing (e.g., divine election/foreknowledge, non-obediential communion) that lack this proof condition. This is refinement of extension/boundary, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary centers experiential intimacy/communion as the knowledge itself (with obedience secondary/evidential), so elevating 'proven by obedience' may over-narrow or reify one alternative into the definition.
